title: WHEN GOD SAYS NO TO A GOOD DESIRE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time I pleaded with the Lord: "Sovereign Lord, you have begun to show to your servant your greatness and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do the deeds and mighty works you do? Let me go over and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that fine hill country and Lebanon." - Deut 3:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we glimpse Moses' heart in a deeply personal moment. He pleaded with God to let him cross the Jordan and see the good land he had journeyed toward for forty years. It was a good and understandable desire. Moses had led the people faithfully through the wilderness; surely he longed to set foot in the Promised Land himself. His prayer is full of worship, marveling at God's greatness, and then his honest request: "Let me go over and see the good land."

There is something tender and human about this. Moses wanted something good, and he brought his desire openly to God in prayer. He did not sulk or demand; he pleaded, honestly and reverently. This is an example for us — we can bring our deepest longings to God, even when we are not sure He will grant them. Prayer is the right place for our honest desires.

Yet, as we will see, God's answer to this good desire was no. Moses would not enter the land, because of an earlier act of disobedience. This reminds us of a truth we all must face: sometimes God says no, even to good things we deeply want. Not every heartfelt desire is granted, even for God's faithful servants.

This can be hard to accept, but we can trust that God's no is never cruel or arbitrary. He sees what we cannot, and His purposes are wise and good, even when they disappoint us. Jesus Himself, in Gethsemane, prayed for the cup to pass yet surrendered to the Father's will (Matt 26:39). We can bring our desires honestly to God, and then trust His answer, knowing that His wisdom and love are always at work, even in the no.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you bring your honest desires to God in prayer, even the uncertain ones?
2. How do you respond when God says no to something good you wanted?
3. How does Jesus' surrender in Gethsemane help you trust God's answers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, I bring my honest desires to You in prayer. Help me to trust Your wisdom even when Your answer is no, knowing that Your purposes are always loving and good, as I follow Jesus who surrendered to Your will. Amen.
